caption: The drawing is a technical sketch rendered in black ink on a light tan or off-white background, depicting detailed views and dimensions of a wooden chair. There are three main views: the seat plan (top view) at the upper left, a rear view of the chair below that, and a side view to the right. The seat plan shows a trapezoidal seat with the front edge measuring 22 inches and the rear 19 inches. The rear view illustrates a chair with four horizontal curved slats on the backrest and legs that taper outwards, along with crossbars near the base. The rear legs are 16¾ inches apart, and the overall height to the top of the backrest is 34½ inches. The side view reveals a slightly arched backrest and a flat, rectangular seat, supported by straight legs and cross braces; various vertical and horizontal dimensions are indicated by dashed and solid lines. There are numerous handwritten notes and measurements, including labeling for "Front," "Rear," and specific heights or widths, as well as a label indicating the drawing’s association with the Brooklyn Museum, the scale (⅛ inch = 1 inch), the drafter’s name, and the date (March 18, 1936).
title: Hitchcock Chair
